result:
I fixed the "Load more" bug in `src/server/repositories/_paging.ts`. I haven't added a regression test for the tie case, and I haven't reproduced your bulk-import scenario. The existing suite passes (617 tests).

The cursor predicate only asked for rows with a `createdAt` (or `occurredAt`) strictly older than the last row shown. Every row stamped at the same instant as that last row was therefore skipped. A bulk import or a burst of assignments stamps all its rows with one timestamp, which is why only those entries went missing.

The predicate now resumes strictly after the cursor row in the same order the queries already sort by (timestamp descending, then id descending). It takes rows with an older timestamp, plus rows with the same timestamp and a smaller id.

The fix is in the shared helper, so it also covers the project issue list, the notification inbox and the audit log. Comments, projects, members and search results had the same flaw and are fixed too. Every query still filters by workspace before applying the cursor, so a page can't include another workspace's entries.
